newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stronger Treasuries help Bunds overcome worries.
newsitem.headline: Stronger Treasuries help Bunds overcome worries.

text.p: Bund futures climbed in late trade as stronger Treasuries helped the market overcome ongoing worries about revaluation of German official reserves and the future of European monetary union (EMU).
The DTB Bund future was up 17 basis points in late trade to 100.67, just off its high of the day.
Bunds were little affected by German unemployment data for May which rose 56,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.358 million.
Germany's unemployment situation was worse than expected and fanned expectations that Bonn will have a hard time trimming its budget deficit to qualify for EMU.
Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing called the unemployment data "more than disappointing," adding that they were a bad sign for tax revenues.
The market was little affected by the figures, however, because of leaks of the data over the last couple of days.
Traders said they expected Bunds to remain on edge next week, likely stuck in a range on Monday roughly between 100.40 to 100.80. Uncertainty should be the watchword.
The Bundesbank, for example, will discuss Bonn's plans to revalue German official reserves at its regular council meeting on Thursday.
There was no word yet if the central bank will make a public statement on the subject.

Several economic indicators are also due, but will be less important with no change in German monetary policy expected. Final may consumer prices are due early in the week and wholesale prices around the middle of the week.
The Amsterdam summit on June 16 and 17, meanwhile, should further add to the market's worries with many expecting the French to try and water down the "stability pact" meant to ensure a stable euro.
The benchmark cash 10-year Bund climbed to 101.54 from 101.22 on the day and the yield fell to 5.79 percent.
The yield curve, meanwhile, flattened by five basis points as the spread between two- and 10-year maturities fell to 226 basis points.
